evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:826-846 — `get_categories` (drives the reality-web homepage "Browse by category" tiles on the sk/cs/de/en portal) maps every `property_type` to a hardcoded SLOVAK label via `label_for_property_type` (listings.rs:823-846): apartment=>"Byty", house=>"Domy", land=>"Pozemky", commercial=>"Komerčné priestory", office=>"Kancelárie", garage=>"Garáže", parking=>"Parkovanie", storage=>"Sklady", with a `capitalize(other)` fallback for unknown types.

The doc comment at listings.rs:765-766 claims "Labels are returned in Slovak (primary market) — the frontend has its own i18n fallback if a label is missing." That justification is misleading: `label_for_property_type` NEVER returns an empty/missing label (the `other => capitalize(other)` arm guarantees a non-empty string for every input), so the promised frontend "missing-label fallback" can never trigger. A cs/de/en visitor therefore either sees Slovak category names, or the frontend must ignore the server `label` entirely and re-localize from `property_type` — in which case the `label` field is dead weight shipped in every response.

Impact: LOW (cosmetic i18n leak on a public marketing surface; no data/security impact). Confidence medium: the server behaviour is confirmed by static read; whether cs/de/en users actually SEE the Slovak text depends on whether reality-web renders `CategoryCount.label` or re-keys off `CategoryCount.property_type` (not runtime-confirmed here). Landable backend-only fix (no build-time codegen touched): either (a) drop the `label` field and let the client localize from the stable `property_type` enum (mirrors how the rest of the portal handles enum display), or (b) return a per-locale label keyed off an `Accept-Language`/`locale` query param. Option (a) is the smaller, safer change and removes the misleading comment.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:472-480 — the public `get_suggestions` handler (GET /api/v1/listings/suggestions, autocomplete/search-suggestions surface) returns `popular_searches` as a HARDCODED three-element vec: ["2-izbový byt Bratislava", "Dom Košice", "Pozemok Žilina"]. The `cities` half of the response is real (derived from `portal_repo.get_nearby_cities`), but `popular_searches` is a static stub shipped on a production public endpoint — it is not derived from any search-frequency/analytics data, so it is not actually 'popular', and it never changes regardless of market activity.

Two problems compound: (1) completeness — the field's name promises data-driven popular searches but delivers a fixed literal, so the feature is effectively unimplemented behind a real-looking API contract; (2) i18n — the three strings are Slovak-only literals on a sk/cs/de/en portal, so a cs/de/en visitor's suggestion box shows Slovak example queries.

Impact: LOW (a public marketing/UX surface; no data or security impact). Confidence medium (static read is definitive on the stub; user-visible effect depends on whether reality-web renders `popular_searches`). Landable backend-only fix: either wire `popular_searches` to a real source (e.g. a top-N aggregation over recent saved-search / search-event rows, or the existing search-analytics tables), or, if that data is not yet available, drop the field from the response contract rather than shipping a hardcoded Slovak stub. If kept as a placeholder, at minimum localize per request locale.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:632 — `RichListingSummary.slug` (returned by the public /api/v1/listings/featured endpoint and consumed by the reality-web homepage to build listing URLs) is set to `slug: r.id.to_string()`, i.e. the raw listing UUID. The field is documented at listings.rs:523 ("URL slug — currently the listing UUID stringified (no slug column yet)") and listings.rs:629-631 ("No slug column on listings yet — the frontend treats the path").

For a PUBLIC real-estate portal where organic search traffic is a primary acquisition channel, UUID-based canonical URLs (/listings/8f3c...-uuid) are an SEO and shareability liability: no keyword signal in the path, opaque/untrustworthy-looking links in social shares and SERPs, and no human-readable fallback. This is acknowledged tech debt rather than a latent crash, but it is a concrete, business-relevant completeness gap on the public surface and is currently un-tracked as a backlog vector.

Impact: LOW (SEO/UX, no correctness/security risk). Confidence medium (behaviour confirmed by static read; SEO impact is well-established for real-estate portals but not measured here). Landable but multi-part: (1) add a `slug` column to `listings` (migration) populated from title + city + short-id (e.g. `3-izbovy-byt-bratislava-8f3c`), backfill existing rows, and enforce uniqueness; (2) return that column here instead of `r.id.to_string()`; (3) accept slug OR uuid in `get_listing` for backward-compatible links. Because it spans a migration + query change + generated-response shape, an implementer should scope it as a small story rather than a one-line fix — flagged here so it enters the backlog with the right size estimate.
